summary: This note covers the top of the 2007 NBA draft, focusing on the first three picks. Greg Oden, a freshman from Ohio State, went first overall to the Portland Trail Blazers but missed the 2007-08 season after microfracture surgery. Kevin Durant, also a freshman from Texas, went second to the Seattle SuperSonics and won Rookie of the Year, while Al Horford went third to the Atlanta Hawks. The note contrasts Durant and Horford's solid All-Star careers with Oden's injury-plagued years.
one_line: Overview of the top three picks in the 2007 NBA draft: Greg Oden, Kevin Durant, and Al Horford, and how their careers unfolded.
key_facts: Greg Oden, a freshman from Ohio State University, was drafted first overall by the Portland Trail Blazers in the 2007 NBA draft.
The Portland Trail Blazers won the draft lottery before selecting Greg Oden first overall.
Greg Oden missed the 2007-08 season due to microfracture surgery on his right knee during the pre-season.
Kevin Durant, a freshman from the University of Texas, was drafted second overall by the Seattle SuperSonics.
Kevin Durant won the Rookie of the Year Award for the 2007-08 season.
Greg Oden and Kevin Durant became the first freshmen to be selected with the top two picks in the draft.
Al Horford, the son of former NBA player Tito Horford, was drafted third overall by the Atlanta Hawks.
Kevin Durant and Al Horford enjoyed solid All-Star careers.
Greg Oden was beset by numerous microfracture surgeries on both knees.
Greg Oden played only 82 games from 2008 to 2010 due to his knee problems.
